# storctl

> storctl is a single-file, curl-runnable Bash utility that mounts SMB/CIFS,
> NFS, iSCSI and NVMe-oF storage on Linux, verifies it, and persists it across
> reboots with fstab or systemd. No Python, daemon or compiled binary.

Repository: https://github.com/iadityaharsh/storctl
Documentation: https://iadityaharsh.github.io/storctl/
Version: 1.0.2
License: MIT

Canonical install command:

bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://iadityaharsh.github.io/storctl/storctl.sh)"

## What it does

- Installs missing protocol clients: cifs-utils, nfs-common/nfs-utils,
  open-iscsi, nvme-cli.
- Mounts SMB/CIFS, NFS, iSCSI and NVMe-oF storage after validating input.
- Lists SMB shares with smbclient and NFS exports with showmount, then lets the
  user select from a menu, with manual entry as a fallback.
- Reuses previously saved SMB credentials, accepts new credentials, or uses
  guest access; saved passwords are never displayed.
- Shows the storctl brand mark in the TUI header and main menu title.
- Formats blank devices as ext4, xfs, btrfs, f2fs, FAT32/vfat, exFAT or NTFS,
  installing the matching mkfs tool on demand and mounting immediately after.
- Persists mounts with a managed /etc/fstab block, x-systemd.automount, a
  generated NVMe-oF systemd unit, and iSCSI node.startup=automatic.
- Verifies mounts with findmnt and rolls back on failure.
- Never formats automatically; formatting requires an explicit choice and the
  ERASE confirmation.
- Stores config in ~/.config/storctl and credentials in
  /etc/storctl/credentials (mode 0600).

## Supported platforms

Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE, Raspberry Pi OS, Proxmox VE and other
systemd-based Linux distributions. Package installation supports apt, dnf,
pacman and zypper.
